newsitem.title: USA: First of America sees Q4 gain.
newsitem.headline: First of America sees Q4 gain.

text.p: First of America Bank Corp said Tuesday it expects to post a gain of $0.25 to $0.30 a share in the fourth quarter, as gains from branch sales offset restructuring costs.
The $22 billion bank holding company said it expects to post charges for severance costs from job reductions and write-downs on properties and other intangibles.
Company spokesman Tony Thompson said the number of layoffs has not been finalized, but it might be about a few hundred.
The firm has some 12,000 employees in Michigan, Indiana, Illinois, Florida, North Carolina and Arizona.

The company said it told employees on Monday about operational changes to further realign to a line-of-business focus from a geographic one, to devote more resources to sales incentives and training, to reduce the cost of delivering products and services, and to boost prospects for profitability.

Beginning in early 1997, 5,000 more employees will move to a pay system that includes sales incentives, and by year-end all employees who have customer contact will be on an incentive or commission pay program.
The firm said it has put in place changes to management incentives to more closely align employees' and directors' interests with those of shareholders, it said.

The trust and financial services, and consumer finance and mortgage services business will remain unchanged, but in 1997 other aspects will be shifted into two divisions instead of the four banks they previously operated from, it said.

The commercial function will center around relationship management, including commercial sales, lending and deposits, as well as commercial mortgages. A consumer unit will be responsible for consumer and small business deposits, lending and branch operations.
